analysis: Examined the two changes in this batch. (1) docs/reference/configuration.md: the only changed lines are head 401-402, which document two new Qwen MTP env controls (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY). Both are documentation only, and both are stated as not forwarded to LaunchAgents, so installed daemons keep source defaults. The rest of the file is unchanged context. Nothing here changes attestation, key custody, coordinator/provider wire behavior or cache encryption; the entries describe MTP scheduling and decode behavior (T-007/TB-007 surface, no new trust claim). Whether the underlying code in libs/mlx-swift-lm matches the documentation is outside the supplied evidence. (2) provider-swift/Sources/ProviderBenchmark/RuntimeConcurrencyBenchmark.swift is a new benchmark-only file (lines 1-226). It runs concurrent greedy decode on public prompts supplied by the CLI, using the production slot construction with prefix caches disabled via RuntimeGenerationBenchmark.prefixCacheDisabledEnvironment() and requirePersistentKey false. Batch sizes are bounded to 1...64, maxTokens to <=131072, and the prompt to 4 MiB. It does not touch the coordinator WebSocket, App Attest, or serving authorization, and it persists nothing besides emitting a JSON report to its caller. It does not read consumer data, and the report holds the prompt SHA-256 rather than prompt text. It does shut down the session and release the container, with error-path handling so that unproven retirement keeps resources. A step-profile table is written to stderr only when CBV2_STEP_PROFILE is enabled. Residual questions for integration: the benchmark's use of the Benchmarking SPI (makeBenchmarkSession with requirePersistentKey false) is only a harness concern if the benchmark target is not shipped to providers. The CLI wiring that exposes this benchmark is not in this batch. No concrete security regression identified.
